en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Second Chapter
The Discussion on Cessation.
Are there two cessations? Yes.
"Are there two cessations of suffering?
"One should not say so... [and so on] ...
"Are there two cessations of suffering?"
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are there two truths of cessation?
One should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Are there two truths of cessation?
Yes. Are there two truths of suffering? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … “Are there two truths of cessation? Yes.
"Are there two truths of origination?
"One should not say so... "...Are there two truths of cessation? "One should not say so."
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are there two truths of the path?
One should not say so … [and so on] …
Are there two truths of cessation?
Yes. Are there two refuges? ... [and so on] ...
Two refuges… two shelters… two final resorts…
Are there two kinds of deathlessness … two kinds of the deathless … two kinds of Nibbāna?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … “Are there two Nibbānas? Yes.
Is there a state of high and low, inferior and superior, excellence and deficiency, a boundary, a division, a line, or an interval between the two types of Nibbāna?
One should certainly not say so… [as before]… Are there two cessations?
“Yes.
“But surely, when formations have ceased through non-reflection, it is through reflection that they are brought to cessation?
“Yes.”
If volitional formations that have ceased without reflection are brought to cessation through reflection, then indeed it should not be said:
"There are two kinds of cessation.
It should not be so stated.
“Are there two kinds of cessation?”— Yes.
But are not conditioned phenomena that have ceased through lack of reflection utterly broken, and are not conditioned phenomena that have ceased through reflection also utterly broken?
“Yes.
“If both formations that have ceased without reflection and formations that have ceased through reflection are utterly broken, then indeed, sir, you must say:
‘There are two kinds of cessation.’”
Are there two kinds of cessation? Yes.
Are formations that have ceased through analytical reflection also ceased by means of the Noble Path? Yes.
“Yes.
“Are formations that have ceased through lack of reflection ceased by means of the Noble Path?
“One should not say so” … [and so on] …
Are there two kinds of cessation?
Yes. Are conditioned phenomena that have ceased through analytical reflection not to arise again? Yes.
“Yes,” you say.
“Then conditioned phenomena that have ceased through lack of reflection do not arise again?
You must not say so … [and so on].
Therefore, it should not be said that "there are two cessations.
The Discussion on Cessation is finished.
The Second Chapter.
Its summary verse:
Taking [food] from another, ignorance,
Doubt, causing others to cross over,
verbal expression, the nutriment of suffering,
and the persistence of the mind in the fiery pit.
Gradual realization,
conventional usage, and the peak of cessation.
